messages:
Maya: heads-up — seeing a steady increase in US customer requests being routed to EU for tier=gold starting ~09:10 UTC. latency up ~120ms and cost spike. 
Devin: annoying, any idea what's triggering cross-region? policy change?
Sana: checking routing logs now — initial hit goes to model:open-llama-13b-v2 (us), fallback goes to open-llama-13b-v1-quant (eu) because of an autoscale mismatch. then request is re-routed back to us for ensembling. looks like a two-hop fallback.
Lucas: Two-hop? so fallback -> variant that isn't compatible -> bounce back to original region? that would create extra KV loads and double tokens.
Maya: exactly. sequences: request -> us:model-v2 -> capacity shortage triggers fallback to eu:quant-v1 -> quant-v1 fails compatibility check and triggers variant-eject -> smart-router retries to us:ensemble-v2. latency and cost are stacking.
infra-bot: ALERT: route-flap detected for tier=gold between us-west1 and eu-west1. 2685 events in last 15m.
Devin: can we see the router decision tree for one of these traces?
Sana: paste of a trace: ```
trace_id=tx-9f3a
step1: route_decision: us-west1 model=open-llama-13b-v2
step2: backend_response=THROTTLE
step3: fallback_choice=eu-west1 model=open-llama-13b-v1-quant
step4: backend_response=INCOMPATIBLE_KV_CACHE
step5: eject_variant -> route_decision: us-west1 model=open-llama-13b-ensemble-v2
step6: success
```
Evan: that INCOMPATIBLE_KV_CACHE is our bug — quant variant uses different KV key format and router doesn't check compatibility before routing.
Lucas: ouch. so the router should be able to check variant.compatible_with[kv_format] before sending.
Maya: short-term mitigation: can we add a circuit-breaker rule that prevents cross-region fallback for tier=gold and uses local degraded model instead?
Devin: yes — I can push a temp policy: ```
policies:
  - id: no-cross-region-fallback-gold
    match: "customer.tier == 'gold' && region != request.region"
    action: "deny_fallback_to_cross_region"
    ttl: 30m
```
Sana: also recommend pinning active gold customers to current model variant until we patch compatibility check. I'll open a console action to pin-by-customer.
Maya: please do both. also we need better telemetry: our route logs didn't include variant_id in the top-level routing span, so it's hard to query how often incompatibility happens.
Lucas: note to infra team: add variant_id and kv_schema_version to routing span and to the Kibana routing index.
Evan: I'll take the compatibility check fix — patch router to validate candidate.variant.kv_schema == request.kv_schema before committing fallback. rolling a small canary in us-west1.
deploy-bot: starting canary rollout of router@patch-compat-check to us-west1 (canary=5%).
Maya: monitoring dashboards - can someone add a row to the routing-health dashboard with metric: sum(route_flap_count) by region,variant and add an alert if >100 in 10m for tier=gold?
Sana: creating dashboard change now and will add alert threshold.
Devin: after policy pushed: temp policy is live. initial telemetry shows cross-region fallbacks dropped ~93% in the last 3m for affected customers.
Evan: canary looks clean so far. patch merged to main and will deploy to eu-west1 next. compatibility tests added to preflight.
Lucas: follow-up UX ask: Console rollout UI should show when a fallback policy is active per-customer and let SEs pin/unpin variants from the customer page. Right now that action is buried in the model-actions panel.
Maya: agreed — filing a product ticket for rollout UX with screenshots of current flow. prioritize for next sprint.
Sana: final checklist: 1) policy temporary deny applied (done), 2) pin customers (in progress), 3) router compat check deployed (in progress), 4) logging fields added (todo), 5) dashboard alert (done).
Maya: thanks all. after eu deploy we'll lift the temporary policy and monitor for any residual bounce. please add any regression traces to the thread. :thumbsup:
